Good -- no additional scroll-snap in the packages. I now have a complete picture. Here is the full analysis: --- ## Summary of Findings ### 1. Root/Index Page **File:** `/Users/samforeman/projects/saforem2/sam.onl/web/src/pages/index.astro` The page wraps everything in the `` component and renders three sections inside a `
` element, plus a fixed VimNavigation overlay: ```astro
``` --- ### 2. Layout File **File:** `/Users/samforeman/projects/saforem2/sam.onl/web/src/layouts/Layout.astro` This is a minimal shell. It: - Imports `@/styles/global.css` (the master stylesheet). - Sets up ``, `` (meta, fonts, theme detection), ``. - Uses `` in the body -- the index page's content is injected here. - Contains inline scripts for: theme persistence (localStorage), Mermaid SVG sizing/rendering, focus management. - No layout-level scroll or snap CSS; all of that is on the page itself. --- ### 3. Scroll-Snap Implementation (Complete) There are exactly **three** files with `scroll-snap` rules, working together in a two-tier system: #### A. The scroll container -- `index.astro` (global style) ```css main { height: 100vh; scroll-snap-type: y proximity; /* <-- enables vertical snap, "proximity" mode */ display: flex; flex-direction: column; overflow-y: auto; overflow-x: hidden; scrollbar-width: thin; scrollbar-color: var(--foreground1) var(--background2); } section, header { scroll-snap-align: start; /* <-- each top-level section/header is a snap point */ display: flex; flex-direction: column; } header { min-height: 100vh; /* <-- Intro takes full viewport */ } ``` Key design choice: `scroll-snap-type: y proximity` means snapping only kicks in when the user is already close to a snap boundary. It does not forcefully lock the user to discrete pages. #### B. Gallery section -- `Gallery.astro` ```css .project-scroll-marker { min-height: 100vh; scroll-snap-align: start; flex: none; background: var(--crust); } ``` The Gallery section has internal scroll markers (invisible `div.project-scroll-marker` elements) that each take `100vh` of height. They act as sub-snap-points within the Gallery's tall container (`min-height: 200vh+`). The visible content is `position: sticky; top: 0` so it pins to the viewport while the markers scroll past underneath. A scroll listener updates which project row is shown. #### C. FeatureThemes section -- `FeatureThemes.astro` ```css .snap { scroll-snap-align: start; height: 100vh; width: 100vw; } ``` Same pattern as Gallery: the section is `min-height: 500vh`. Invisible `.snap` divs (each `100vh`) create sub-snap-points. The visible preview is `position: sticky; top: 0`. A scroll listener swaps the active theme on each snap. #### D. Scroll utility -- `web/src/utils/scroll.ts` This file provides cross-browser scroll-snap event handling: - **Chromium:** Uses native `scrollsnapchange` event on `
`. - **Firefox:** Falls back to `scrollend` event + manual intersection detection via `determineSnapTarget()`. - **Safari:** Falls back to raw `scroll` event + `determineSnapTarget()`. `determineSnapTarget()` finds the first element matching a CSS selector whose bounding rect intersects the viewport. --- ### 4. Status Line Component **File:** `/Users/samforeman/projects/saforem2/sam.onl/web/src/components/landing/sections/Intro.astro` The status line is built directly inside the `
` in the Intro section, at lines 46-71: ```astro NORMAL  main sam.onl utf-8 Top 1:1 ``` This mimics a Neovim/Vim statusline with: - Mode indicator (`NORMAL` in blue) - Git branch (` main`) - Filename (`sam.onl`) -- flex-grows to fill center - Right side: encoding (`utf-8`), scroll position (`Top`), cursor position (`1:1`) --- ### 5. Status Line CSS Also in `/Users/samforeman/projects/saforem2/sam.onl/web/src/components/landing/sections/Intro.astro`, lines 119-139: ```css #statusline { position: absolute; bottom: 0; width: 100%; height: 2lh; background-color: var(--background0); box-shadow: 0 -1lh 0 0 var(--mantle); } @media (max-width: 50ch) { #statusline-right { display: none; /* hides utf-8 / Top / 1:1 on narrow screens */ } } ``` The status line is absolutely positioned at the bottom of `#intro` (which is `position: relative`). The `box-shadow: 0 -1lh 0 0 var(--mantle)` creates a solid bar of color _above_ the status line (effectively a 1-line-height "tabline" area in the `--mantle` color). Additionally, the `@webtui/theme-everforest` package defines dedicated status-line color tokens: - `/Users/samforeman/projects/saforem2/sam.onl/packages/theme-everforest/src/base.css` defines `--statusline1`, `--statusline2`, `--statusline3` variables (though the Intro component does not currently reference them -- it uses the generic badge variant colors instead). --- ### 6. Page Sections Structure -- How Snap Points Are Created The snap scroll architecture is a **two-tier system**: #### Tier 1: Top-level sections (snap container = `
`) ```
← scroll-snap-type: y proximity; height: 100vh; overflow-y: auto ├──
← scroll-snap-align: start; min-height: 100vh ├──
← scroll-snap-align: start └──
← scroll-snap-align: start
``` Every `
` and `
` is a snap point. The `
` element is the scroll container (not `` or ``). #### Tier 2: Internal sub-snap-points (within tall sections) Some sections (Gallery, FeatureThemes -- not currently in the index page's `
` but part of the landing component library) use a "tall section + sticky content + invisible markers" pattern: ```
← overall snap point for tier 1 ├── ← position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100vh │ └── (the actual UI) ├──
← scroll-snap-align: start; height: 100vh ├──
← scroll-snap-align: start; height: 100vh └── ...
``` As the user scrolls through these tall sections, the visible content stays pinned (sticky), while the invisible marker divs scroll past. Each marker is a snap point.
